key_insight: A physics-informed machine learning framework can predict porosity defects in high-power laser beam welding across aluminum and steel by using dimensionless, physically meaningful features tied to keyhole stability and bubble capture.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable process planning and defect control in laser welding of different metals, helping improve weld quality and reduce porosity-related failure risk.
method: Conducted systematic LBW experiments over a broad parameter space for aluminum and steel.
Used a validated multiphysics simulation to capture molten pool behavior and keyhole dynamics.
Built a universal ML model with dimensionless physical features to predict porosity ratio.
evidence_signal: The model achieved a general root mean square error of 1.35 and identified Stokes number and keyhole aspect ratio as the most influential factors.
watch_item: Performance depends on the validity of the simulation-informed features and may require recalibration when extending to new alloys, thicknesses, or laser/process conditions.
paper_title: Universal physics-informed machine learning framework for the prediction of porosity defects in high-power laser beam welding with different metallic materials
